answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to earn a non-transferable work record before it can move value: new agents start with a tiny limit and only gain higher limits after peers verify completed jobs, so a flood of fake identities stays stuck at the bottom like a ripple that never becomes a river. Reputation decays when idle and is slashed on fraud, so an attacker must pay real compute and time for every fake, while honest agents keep a nebula of distinct, checkable histories that cannot be bought or copied in bulk.
